name: Sleeping Porch Cluster
description: A screened or open porch used for sleeping, attached to a bedroom and treated as part of it. A public-health idea before it was an architectural one — fresh air was the tuberculosis treatment — and it is the best cheap bedroom in a hot climate.

internal_rules.statement: Entered from the bedroom it serves, not from a corridor. A sleeping porch off a hall is a porch.
Depth not less than 8 ft — a bed is 6 ft 3 in and needs a passage beside it.
Oriented to the prevailing summer breeze and away from the afternoon sun; east and north-east are the useful aspects.
Roofed by the main roof or a continuous extension of it, never by a separate applied canopy.
Where it is enclosed later — and it nearly always is — the enclosure must keep the opening proportion, or the elevation acquires a band of squat windows where a void used to be.

attaches_to.position: the pop-up room itself, which is a sleeping porch lifted into the breeze
over the front porch or at a rear corner
the upper piazza, which serves the same purpose without being named for it

expansion_logic: Enclose it and it becomes a room, which is what happened to nearly all of them after air conditioning. Doing that well means keeping the opening rhythm.
servicing_strategy: No heat, no plumbing, and screens rather than glass. Adding conditioning converts it into a room and it should then be detailed as one.

style_variation.note: Canonical, and part of the style's health argument as much as its plan.
Common on the 1910-1930 examples and almost always enclosed since.
The upper piazza does the job and always did, two centuries before the idea was medicalised.
